request: Repair the observed Windows transient EPERM replacing a Codex registration journal after closed file handles, while preserving expected-snapshot conflict detection and owned-file cleanup.
decisions: Retry existing-file atomic rename only on Windows and only for EPERM or EBUSY.
Allow at most five rename attempts, separated by 25, 50, 100 and 200 milliseconds, for 375 milliseconds total maximum retry waiting.
Repeat safe destination snapshot validation before each attempt and preserve the original expected bytes, existence and mode across all retries.
A changed or unsafe destination aborts with the existing conflict/security errors. Never delete the destination, widen permissions, disable locks, or adopt new expected bytes.
Keep missing-destination no-overwrite link creation and finally-based owned temporary-file cleanup unchanged.
Tests inject faults only inside sequential, awaited scopes and restore fs.rename and the process platform descriptor before fixture cleanup.
No actual Codex credentials, user configuration or model calls are used by the regression fixtures.

tests.result: RED: 3 failures and 1 pass. The probe executes the actual snapshot/replace source functions after Node TypeScript transformation; transient Windows recovery, intervening-edit conflict, and bounded retry assertions failed as expected.
GREEN: all 4 focused tests pass. Transient EPERM/EBUSY recovery, conflict preservation, bounded exhaustion/cleanup, and no non-Windows retry were observed.

Four public-API regression tests added. Full-module execution with pinned dependencies and actual Windows integration is pending the parent integration run; no Windows PASS is claimed by this child record.

roadmap_updates.notes: Reliability repair retains atomic writes, conflict checks, backups and existing scope. No broader configuration acceptance credit is awarded.
Codex registration retry behavior receives focused regression coverage; release/platform acceptance still depends on the integrated exact-head gates.

limitations: A persistent OS lock still fails after the bounded retry budget; no ACL changes or destination deletion are attempted.
Safe snapshot checks and rename remain separate OS calls, so this is not a handle-anchored defense against a hostile local writer ignoring the ownership lock.
The parent integration owner must run full TypeScript/build, registration tests and the previously failing Windows suite, then perform final source/roadmap review.
